answer: Staking a refundable bond per identity makes Sybil attacks expensive: each new agent must lock tokens that are slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning a meadow of fake identities drains the attacker's own capital instead of being free. Honest agents earn the bond back plus rewards, while a relic of past misbehavior follows the stake, not just the name. Reputation then grows in a spiral — verified work raises the bond's yield, so one strong identity pays far more than a hundred cheap fakes.
